scope: Test generic candidate diversity, valid whole-turn rollout scoring, and non-route-specific leaf survival value before training another student.

protocol.holdout_note: These are fresh Teacher diagnostic seeds, not policy holdout evaluations. No BC/PPO checkpoint was trained from them.

implementation_repairs: Rollout Teacher now completes an actor prefix with legal fallback actions before calling submit_plan; rollout_rejections stayed at 0.
Candidate selection supports top, diverse, and all modes, with generic structural and target diversity diagnostics.
Turn-level beam pruning and leaf ranking can include a generic nonterminal state value based on Boss HP, ally damage, deaths, and turn progress.
Teacher CLI exposes generic leaf and survival weights without naming a status, identity, skill, or E.G.O route.

Teacher samples can optionally downweight failed episodes by generic final-state quality, omit rows below a quality threshold, and apply generic one-actor counterfactual score margins; legacy weighting remains the default.

candidate_recall.reference: uncapped first-turn heuristic Teacher on the same initial state
candidate_recall.interpretation: At least on the common first turn, cap=6 did not remove the uncapped Teacher's chosen actions. Candidate pruning is therefore not the primary demonstrated bottleneck for this scene.

conclusion: The rollout implementation bug was real and is fixed: the previous implementation sent incomplete partial plans to submit_plan, so every partial rollout was rejected.
Generic diversity plus leaf value materially improves damage and survival, and the survival-weighted rollout increases fresh full-HP Teacher wins from 0-1/50 to 3/50.
This is not yet enough successful data for BC/PPO. All successful episodes still have axis_ok_rate=0 and direct_burst_rate=1, so the intended delayed route has not emerged.

The next bottleneck is search value/credit quality and demonstration selection, not another terminal reward tweak. Keep successful and near-successful trajectories separate from ordinary failures, then add counterfactual or top-k plan credit before training a new policy.
